acceptance_criteria.criterion: PollingManager.restart(intervalSeconds) stops the current interval and starts a new one with the given interval.
GET /api/config/polling returns { gitPollingIntervalSeconds: 30 } when using the default config.
PUT /api/config/polling with { seconds: 60 } persists the value to config.json, updates in-memory appConfig.gitPollingIntervalSeconds, restarts the polling manager, and returns the updated value.
PUT /api/config/polling with { seconds: 5 } returns HTTP 400 with a descriptive error message.
PUT /api/config/polling with non-numeric, fractional, or missing seconds returns HTTP 400.
Existing registerConfigRoutes callers that do not pass pollingManager continue to work without error (parameter is optional).

summary: Reviewed 5 files: src/server/routes/config.ts, src/server/pollingManager.ts, src/server/index.ts, src/config/config.ts, src/server/requestUtils.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (noted), 3 Low (noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: OWASP A01 (Broken Access Control) — CLEAR. The PUT /api/config/polling endpoint requires no elevated privilege check because this is a local tool (server binds to 127.0.0.1 only — see index.ts L163). No IDOR or path-traversal risk from the numeric-only `seconds` field. Credentials DELETE decodes the :host path param via decodeURIComponent() and checks existence before mutating — correct.

OWASP A02 (Cryptographic Failures) — CLEAR. No new cryptographic operations introduced. Git credential tokens are still never returned in plaintext (maskToken() applied on all GET/PUT/DELETE responses). saveConfigField() calls chmodSync(path, 0o600) after every write, restricting config.json to owner-only on POSIX. No cleartext transmission risk for a localhost-only server.

OWASP A03 (Injection) — CLEAR. The `seconds` field is consumed strictly as a JavaScript number (typeof check + isFinite + isInteger guards) and written directly to appConfig.gitPollingIntervalSeconds (a numeric field) and passed to setInterval() as `intervalSeconds * 1000`. No string interpolation into any interpreter. No SQL, OS command, or template injection vector.

OWASP A04 (Insecure Design) — CLEAR for new surface. Validation chain in PUT /api/config/polling is defence-in-depth: typeof number → isFinite → isInteger → >= 10, in that order. The QA agent confirmed that Infinity, -Infinity, NaN, null, undefined, arrays, and fractional values are all rejected. The optional pollingManager guard (line 251) prevents null-dereference when the parameter is absent.

OWASP A05 (Security Misconfiguration) — CLEAR. Server listens on 127.0.0.1 (loopback only). Error responses return { error: string } with no stack traces or internal path leakage. The invalid JSON error truncates the raw body to 120 chars (requestUtils.ts L46) to avoid leaking unexpectedly large payloads in error messages.

OWASP A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components) — No new dependencies introduced by this WP. All changes are in first-party TypeScript source files using Node.js built-ins only (node:http, node:fs, node:path, setInterval/clearInterval). No third-party packages added.

OWASP A07 (Authentication Failures) — Not applicable. This is a local developer tool with no multi-user authentication layer. The loopback-only binding (127.0.0.1) is the intended access control boundary. No session management or auth endpoints were modified.

OWASP A08 (Software & Data Integrity) — CLEAR. No deserialization of complex objects; only a plain JSON number is accepted and stored. saveConfigField() performs a read-modify-write on config.json using the internal writeJsonFile() helper, which serialises with JSON.stringify — no unsafe deserialization path.

OWASP A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring) — INFO. No audit log is emitted when the polling interval is changed. For a local developer tool this is acceptable; however, if the tool ever gains multi-user or remote access, a security event log entry for configuration changes would be warranted.

OWASP A10 (SSRF) — CLEAR. The PUT /api/config/polling endpoint stores a numeric interval used in setInterval(); it does not trigger any outbound HTTP/network call directly. The PollingManager.restart() method only re-arms a timer for the existing git-status polling loop — no user-controlled URL is introduced.

Unbounded upper limit on polling interval (Medium / A04 — Insecure Design / DoS-adjacent). src/server/routes/config.ts L234-242: The PUT /api/config/polling handler enforces a minimum of 10 seconds but no maximum. A value of Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (9,007,199,254,740,991) passes all validation guards and would effectively disable git polling for the life of the process — the PollingManager would schedule a setInterval that never fires in practice. While this is not exploitable remotely (loopback-only), it could lead to an unintentional self-DOS or user confusion. Recommendation: enforce a reasonable upper bound (e.g. 86400 seconds / 24 hours) with a clear error message. This is a Medium finding and does not block approval, but should be tracked for a follow-up.

Input Validation — PASS. All external inputs are validated server-side before any mutation. isPlainObject() guards against array and primitive bodies. The `seconds` field undergoes a 4-step guard chain. The `host` field in credential routes is validated against whitespace/slash injection and prototype-pollution keys.

Data Handling — PASS. gitCredentials tokens are never returned in full; maskToken() exposes only the last 4 characters. config.json is chmoded to 0o600 after every write. The gitPollingIntervalSeconds value stored is a plain integer — no PII or sensitive data concern.

Auth/Authz Patterns — PASS. All new endpoints follow the same access pattern as existing endpoints: loopback-only binding acts as the sole access control boundary, consistent with the rest of the application.
